user.title: Connect to Amber
user.description: Enter an Amber API key. You can create one on Amber's developer page.

site.title: Choose a site
site.description: Choose a site to set up first. The entry is your Amber account; add further sites afterwards with **Add site** on the integration page.

site_name.title: Name this site

data_description.site_name: For example "Home" or "Beach house". If you also use Amber Express, using the same name makes its devices and these easy to match.

These metering channels were found for the NMI ending {nmi}. Usage, cost and feed-in compensation will be imported for each of them.

schedule.title: Import schedule
schedule.description: Amber publishes usage about a day late. Automatic picks a stable time for this installation each morning (between 06:30 and 08:30), with retries 3 and 6 hours later; while the day still isn't published, it retries every 3 hours until 22:00. Once the day is imported, the remaining attempts are skipped.

data_description.fixed_times: Only for fixed times: up to 6 local times, comma separated, for example 07:15, 10:15, 13:15.
data_description.add_to_energy: Shown only when the Energy dashboard has no grid connection yet. Adds one with this site's grid consumption and cost and, with feed-in, the return to grid and compensation (controlled load as a second grid connection). The data appears after the first import.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate with Amber
reauth_confirm.description: Amber rejected the API key for {entry}. Enter a new key for the same account; it must see at least one of the sites set up here (a site it doesn't see is skipped, with a Repairs item).

error.site_not_found: This key sees none of the sites set up here.

settings.title: Import settings
settings.description: Automatic picks a stable time each morning (between 06:30 and 08:30), with retries 3 and 6 hours later; while the day still isn't published, it retries every 3 hours until 22:00.

data.own_fallback: Hourly fallback for grid meters and appliances

data_description.fixed_times: Only for fixed times: up to 6 local times, comma separated, for example 07:15, 10:15, 13:15.
data_description.patience_days: A day that stays empty on this many separate days, while later days have data, is skipped as a gap (default 7).
data_description.revision_days: Days with estimated data are re-checked daily for this many days; if Amber revises them, history is rewritten from that day on (default 14, 0 turns it off).
data_description.usage_mode: Full imports usage every day. Recovery-only imports nothing on a schedule (use the backfill service). Pricing-only writes no usage statistics, only prices and the cost of grid meters and appliances. Switching never deletes statistics; ones no longer updated simply stop.
data_description.price_series: Also write an hourly price series per channel (AUD/kWh). An hourly mean price is not a cost rate. Enabling it fetches the full retention window once (about 13 API calls for 90 days).
data_description.own_fallback: When 5-minute sensor data is no longer available (after about 10 days), price hourly energy at the hour's mean price and flag the day as lower precision. If off, such days are skipped.

bill.title: Bill estimate
bill.description: Estimates your Amber bill for the current billing cycle from the imported usage, plus your daily fixed charges. Enter the rates from your Amber bill's charges summary, excluding GST: see [Finding these on your bill]({bill_help_url}). Only complete imported days count, so the estimate runs a day behind. One-off charges (such as card payment fees) are not included. Leave the billing day empty to turn the estimate off.

data.fixed_statistic: Also write cost including fixed charges

data_description.billing_day: The first day of your bill period (for '28 Aug – 27 Sep', enter 28).
data_description.daily_supply: The Network Daily Supply Charges rate in your bill's charges summary. It already includes metering; don't add the metering line separately.
data_description.amber_subscription: From your bill's Amber Fees section. Enter 0 if your subscription is currently free (for example a first-year offer), and update it when the offer ends.
data_description.other_daily: Optional: any other fixed daily charge on your bill (default 0).
data_description.gst_percent: Added to the daily charges (default 10 %). Amber's usage figures already include GST.
data_description.fixed_statistic: An extra statistic: the import cost plus the fixed charges (including GST), spread over each day's hours. It is built from this integration's own statistics, so it covers the whole history (including history copied from the YAML kit) with no API calls. Select it in the Energy dashboard instead of the cost if you want its totals to match your bill. Changed charges apply from the day after the last imported day.

allowance.title: Export allowance

data_description.allowance_kwh_per_day: kWh a day; the period's allowance is this times its days.
data_description.allowance_totalling: Billing period: exports in the charged period are set against the whole period's allowance (as on the N61 bill). Daily: each day has its own allowance.
data_description.penalty_period: The tariff period name in Amber's data in which exports are charged (solarSponge for N61).

sources.title: Sources
sources.description:
Sensors this site's live estimates can use. Billed figures always come from Amber's usage data.

**Live price** (for Today so far). Found for this site:
{detected}

Until you save this step, the sensors found are used automatically. Clear a field to use no live price for that channel. Prices must be in $/kWh (c/kWh and $/MWh are converted), with the feed-in price positive when you are paid, as both Amber integrations show it.

**Today so far** reads the grid meter's sensors: {meter}.

**Solar production** (optional): your solar system's power and/or cumulative energy sensor, for example from your inverter's integration. **Battery** (optional): the cumulative energy charged into and discharged from your home battery. Used by appliances with solar-aware cost (the energy sensor when both solar sensors are set; both battery sensors are needed).

data_description.solar_power: Optional: a power sensor (W or kW).
data_description.battery_charge: Optional: cumulative energy into the battery.
data_description.battery_discharge: Optional: cumulative energy out of the battery.

marker_mismatch.title: Amber import stopped: marker and statistics disagree
marker_mismatch.description:
The import for {entry} has stopped because its saved position does not match the statistics in the database: {details}.

Nothing has been written. This can happen if statistics were changed or deleted by hand, or the integration's storage was restored from a different backup. Restore a consistent backup, or open an issue with the diagnostics attached.

unexpected_channel.title: Amber reports a new metering channel
unexpected_channel.description:
Usage for {day} on {entry} contains a channel that is not configured: {details}.

This usually means a new meter channel (for example controlled load) was added to your Amber account. Imports are paused so that no data is lost or mis-assigned. Open the site's settings (the cog on the integration, or the pencil on the site) and choose **Refresh channels** to add the channel; imports then continue from {day}.

incomplete_data.title: Amber usage data is incomplete
incomplete_data.description:
Usage for {day} on {entry} failed the completeness check ({reason}): {details}.

Nothing was written for this day. The next attempt will fetch it again; this clears automatically once a complete day is imported.

import_failed.title: Amber import could not be verified
import_failed.description:
{day} was written for {entry} but reading it back did not match: {details}.

The import position was not advanced. The next attempt will rewrite the day.

site_not_found.title: Amber site no longer visible: {site}
site_not_found.description:
The API key of {entry} no longer sees the site {site}, for example because the site was closed or moved to another Amber account. Its import is paused; the account's other sites keep running.

- If the site is closed, delete it: on the integration page, open the site's ⋮ menu and choose Delete. Its statistics are kept.
- If the key should still see it, re-authenticate with a key that does, or reload the integration once Amber shows the site again.

This clears by itself when the key sees the site at the next start or reload.

behind.title: Amber import is behind
behind.description:
After the last scheduled attempt today, {entry} has only reached {last_date} ({days_behind} days behind yesterday). Last run: {status} {reason}

This clears by itself once the import catches up. If it persists for several days, check the status sensor and diagnostics.

user.title: Add a grid meter
user.description:
A grid meter measures the energy flowing through your main supply. Examples: a CT clamp or energy monitor on the mains feed, or the grid meter of an inverter or battery system (such as a Sigenergy system or a Fronius smart meter).

Its import is priced at Amber's billed rate for each 5-minute interval (general, or controlled load), and its export at the feed-in rate, so you see what your meter's readings cost.

Because it measures the same energy Amber bills, the integration compares it each day with Amber's billed totals (reconciliation). That shows calibration drift and dropped readings, and with import and export it also estimates the meter's calibration offset in watts.

Choose the raw sensors as the meter reports them, not ones you have already corrected: the offset is measured from these sensors, so a corrected sensor would feed its own correction back.

data_description.name: For example "Whole house meter". It names the meter's device and sensors.
data_description.import_entity_id: Cumulative energy drawn from the grid (kWh, always rising).
data_description.import_channel: The Amber channel this meter's import is billed on: general, or controlled load for a meter on that circuit.
data_description.export_entity_id: Cumulative energy sent to the grid, priced at the feed-in rate. Leave empty if you have no export, or the meter doesn't report it.

site.title: Choose a site
site.description: This account has several sites. Choose the one this belongs to.

error.not_cumulative_energy: Choose a sensor with device class energy and state class total or total_increasing.
error.sensor_in_use: This sensor is already used by another grid meter, appliance or own sensor. A sensor can be priced only once.
error.same_sensor: Choose different sensors for import and export.

abort.no_import_channel: This site has no general or controlled load channel to price an import on.
abort.no_sites: This account has no sites. Add one with Add site first.

user.title: Add an appliance
user.description:
An appliance is any single energy sensor. Examples: a smart plug, a CT clamp on one circuit, an appliance's own energy sensor (such as a heat pump or hot water system), or an EV charger.

Its energy is priced at Amber's billed rate for each 5-minute interval and recorded as a cost statistic, with sensors for yesterday's energy and cost.

An appliance is not compared with Amber's billed totals: one circuit is only part of what the house draws, so the difference would mean nothing. To compare a meter on the main supply with Amber, add a grid meter instead.

data_description.name: For example "Pool heat pump". It names the appliance's device and sensors.
data_description.entity_id: Cumulative energy used by the appliance (kWh, always rising).
data_description.channel: The Amber channel the appliance is billed on: general, or controlled load if it is on that circuit (for example a hot water system).
data_description.solar_aware: Also record a solar-aware cost statistic (for example "Pool pump cost (solar-aware)"): the part of the appliance's energy covered by the site's solar is valued at the feed-in price (the income given up), the rest at the import price. Needs a solar sensor in the site's Sources and a grid meter with import and export. General channel only.

site.title: Choose a site
site.description: This account has several sites. Choose the one this belongs to.

reconfigure.title: Solar-aware cost
reconfigure.description:
{name}: also record a solar-aware cost statistic and a "Yesterday solar-aware cost" sensor. The part of the appliance's energy covered by the site's solar is valued at the feed-in price (the income given up), and the rest at the import price. The share is the house's for each 5-minute interval, from the grid meter and the solar sensor. The normal cost statistic doesn't change.

Turning it on starts the statistic from the earliest day the sensors' statistics allow (Amber's usage retention at most).

data_description.solar_aware: Needs a solar sensor in the site's Sources and a grid meter with import and export. General channel only.

error.not_cumulative_energy: Choose a sensor with device class energy and state class total or total_increasing.
error.sensor_in_use: This sensor is already used by another grid meter, appliance or own sensor. A sensor can be priced only once.
error.same_sensor: Choose different sensors for import and export.
error.solar_aware_channel: Solar-aware cost is for appliances on the general channel only: a controlled load is metered separately.
error.solar_aware_no_solar: Add the site's solar sensor first (site settings, Sources).
error.solar_aware_no_grid_meter: Add a grid meter with import and export first: the solar share comes from the site's grid import and export.

abort.no_import_channel: This site has no general or controlled load channel to price an appliance on.
abort.no_sites: This account has no sites. Add one with Add site first.
abort.appliance_site_missing: The appliance's site or channel no longer exists.

user.title: Price your own energy sensor
user.description: Choose a cumulative energy sensor (for example CT clamps or a smart plug) and the Amber channel whose billed price applies. Its cost is recorded as a statistic, from the later of the sensor's history start and Amber's retention boundary.

error.not_cumulative_energy: Choose a sensor with device class energy and state class total or total_increasing.
